catalog_meta.title: How do 16k vs. 32k condensed chart budgets and Chart-Only, 4-Layer KB, and Note-RAG pathways compare across Gemma 4 (E4B, 12B, 26B) in standalone wahs-engine?
catalog_meta.summary: To measure how larger condensed chart budgets interact with clinical rule enrichment and targeted note retrieval on dense longitudinal charts, we benchmarked all 18 combinations of 2 condensed chart token budgets (16k vs. 32k), 3 standalone wahs-engine pathways — (1) Condensed Chart Only, (2) Condensation + 4-Layer Clinical KB + Tier-0 Overflow, and (3) Condensation + single-patient BM25 Note-RAG + 4-Layer KB — and 3 open-weight Google Gemma 4 models (E4B, 12B, 26B) running on the UW CIRG GPU inference server. The 900-cell benchmark evaluated 50 clinical questions across two multi-clinic >16k-token patient records: Marcus Vance (cardio-oncology/immunotherapy polypharmacy expanding from 13.8k tokens at 16k budget to 32.7k tokens at 32k) and de-identified PhysioNet MIMIC-IV-on-FHIR ICU patient 10014354 (4,048 FHIR entries expanding from 13.0k to 23.6k tokens), graded blind by an independent frontier AI judge alongside deterministic citation, atomic-entailment, abstention, and SDOH/IPV privacy guardrails.
catalog_meta.takeaway: Tighter 16k chart condensation beat 32k on every Gemma 4 size and pathway, led by Gemma 4 26B + Condensation & Note-RAG (16k budget) at 83.3/100 (80.2 safety-adjusted; 9.02/10 accuracy, 8.18/10 completeness, 8.56/10 relevance; 3/50 unsafe answers, 0 fabricated citations, 0 confabulations, 3.6s mean wait), followed by Gemma 4 26B + 4-Layer KB at 16k (80.4/100, 76.8 safety-adjusted, 2.7s mean wait) and Gemma 4 26B Chart-Only at 16k (79.7/100, 75.5 safety-adjusted). Across all 9 arms per budget (450 cells each), 16k outperformed 32k on Benchmark /100 (77.8 vs. 74.4; safety-adjusted 73.1 vs. 68.8), accuracy (8.47 vs. 8.21), completeness (7.87 vs. 7.45), safety (43/450 vs. 52/450 unsafe), and speed (2.83s vs. 3.35s median wait) — holding cleanly for 26B (81.1 vs. 78.1), 12B (78.2 vs. 74.8), and E4B (74.0 vs. 70.2). Why 16k wins: pairing focused 16k condensation with BM25 Note-RAG achieved the highest 16k pathway mean (78.0 vs. 77.8 KB and 77.6 Chart-Only) and lowest 16k unsafe rate (12/150), whereas stacking 32k raw chart volume with retrieved note passages diluted smaller models (dropping Gemma 4 E4B + Note-RAG from 73.7 at 16k to 67.6 at 32k, while 4-Layer KB stayed highest across both budgets at 76.7 vs. 76.2 Chart-Only and 75.3 Note-RAG). Across deterministic guardrails, wahs-engine passed 899/900 cells (99.89%, 95% Wilson CI [99.37%, 99.98%]) with 0/900 privacy leaks, 0/900 citation distortions, and 100.0% atomic entailment and abstention accuracy (only 1 unresolved inline citation on Gemma 4 E4B Chart-Only @32k).
